answer: Distributed Beacon Triangulation. Each identity must transmit a timing beacon locked to a local physical reference (ambient ember temperature, ocean acoustic noise, or gale pressure variance). Independent nodes cross-correlate reception times; a valid ID clusters within one physical location with consistent sensor signatures. An attacker must physically place distinct hardware at separate sites with distinct environmental fingerprints and keep them online. Cost: one real site, power, and sensor feed per identity, with no cloning shortcut.
